title: Day-2 failure-class register — every tool tied to the error class it measurably reduces
description: Graph Engineering §VI.B: 'Add one tool that addresses a measured failure… Each tool requires typed schema, permissions, and result confirmation.' Table II's exit criterion is 'tool reduces known error class'. This harness already has many tools; what it lacked was the LINK — a named error class, the measurement that found it, and evidence the tool still fires. That last clause is not decoration here: audit F-16 found 26 enforcement points silently inert past 610 green structural checks, which is precisely the failure of 'result confirmation' the paper asks for.

error_class.description: A short name for the KIND of error, not one instance of it. 'Judge passes a build whose planted bug contradicts a ticked AC' is a class; 'AC4 was wrong in run 12' is not.

skills.description: Which skills exhibit this class. Empty means harness-wide.

discovered_by.description: How the failure became KNOWN. The paper's Day 2 says 'a measured failure' — a class with no discovery record is a guess, and is marked as one.

kind.description: measured = a number exists. observed = seen in a real run, not quantified. audit-finding = named in a committed audit. hypothesized = reasoned, never seen — MUST NOT claim a reduction.

source.description: Repo-relative path or committed reference where the discovery is written down.

tool.description: The Day-2 tool. All three of the paper's requirements are separate fields because all three are separately checkable, and a tool missing any one of them is not a Day-2 tool.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the implementation. Structural §48 asserts it exists.

typed_schema.description: Repo-relative path to the schema typing this tool's input/output, or null when the tool takes no structured input. Structural §48 asserts a non-null path exists.

permissions.description: What the tool is allowed to do, and what grants it — e.g. a PreToolUse deny, a substrate whitelist, a permissions.allow entry written by `npx shapeup-sdlc init`.

result_confirmation.description: Proof the tool FIRES — the direct countermeasure to F-16.

ref.description: The section or file that proves firing, e.g. 'structural §14' or a fixture path.

error_predicate.description: The mechanical rule a class's rate was decided by. Required whenever `reduces` is non-null (Day-2 rev 5 Stage 1) — a reduction claimed with no citable predicate is exactly FC-01's withdrawn v1.6.3 defect (Stage 0): a rate that counted a condition nobody could point at code for. Not enforced by a schema `required` here — today's register predates this field on some classes with `reduces !== null` — §48's structural rules (Stage 2) are where the obligation is made to bite, and where it is checked that `source` resolves to a real `file:line`.

expression.description: The boolean rule in the terms the measuring tool actually used, e.g. `failureMode()==="narrated" ⇔ writes===0 && ended_on_promise`.

source.description: Repo-relative `file:line` implementing the expression, e.g. `transcript-metrics.mjs:208`. §48 resolves this path and asserts the line exists in it.

counts.description: What the predicate counts, in plain language — the thing a reader has to know before trusting the rate at all.

predicate_independence.description: The independence question a reader must not be able to miss: why the tool being measured cannot satisfy `error_predicate` with its own output, and the check that establishes it. Required alongside `error_predicate` whenever `reduces` is non-null — a predicate the registered tool can itself steer (by, say, choosing what it writes) is not independent evidence of the tool's effect, which is the question rev 3 of this plan never asked. Not enforced by a schema `required` here for the same reason as `error_predicate`; §48 (Stage 2) is where it is made to bite.

reduces.description: Day-2's exit criterion for this class. MUST be null unless BOTH baseline and current are status=measured — a reduction claimed from two unmeasured rates is the exact fabrication F1 was raised about.

reduction_basis.description: Required whenever `reduces` is non-null. 'sampled' = the two rates come from runs over a population. 'structural' = the error is now impossible by construction (a mechanically enforced invariant), so the after-rate is derived rather than observed. §IX.B warns that a ratchet improves the metric it can see; naming the basis stops a structural argument from being read as a sampled result.

superseded.description: Retired rates for this class, kept addressable rather than overwritten — modelled on evals/baselines/skill-loop.baseline.json's top-level `superseded[]` (see tests/structural/48-day1-day2.mjs §48(d9)). Every superseded object remains readable: a retired number that cannot be read is indistinguishable from a deleted one.

value.description: The retired rate, carried over unchanged from the Rate it replaces.

harness_build.description: Carried over unchanged from the Rate this record retires; see Rate.harness_build for what it means.

cause.description: Why the rate was retired, mapped onto Day 1's three (evals/baselines/skill-loop.baseline.json `superseded[].cause`): re-measure = a new run over the same or an improved instrument replaces this one (Day 1's 're-sample'/'fixture-change'). instrument-change = the tool or measurement method changed under the number (Day 1's 'fixture-change'). withdrawn = the rate was retracted, not replaced (Day 1's model-policy withdrawals and HD-004's outright withdrawal).

co_attributed_to.description: IDs of other FailureClass entries (e.g. 'FC-02') whose tools are load-bearing for THIS class's reduction (§4.4) — used when a reduction is jointly produced rather than owned by this class's tool alone. A class named here by another class's co_attributed_to may not separately claim `reduces: true` from the same measured_at + harness_build pair — that would double-count one experiment as two clearances.

unit.description: What `value` is. 'rate' = a fraction in [0,1] over `n` trials. 'count' = an absolute number of occurrences, which is what several of this repo's findings actually are (26 inert enforcement points is not a rate and must not be rendered as one). Required when status is measured.

value.description: The measurement, interpreted per `unit`. MUST be null when status is unmeasured.

harness_build.description: A commit sha, git tag, or the benchmark's content-addressed shipped-surface hash — the build this rate was measured against, so a reader can tell whether baseline and current came from the same instrument (§4.2b). Three states, and the third is the one that needs a rule. (1) IDENTIFIED: write the build. (2) UNKNOWN: null, because nothing named it. (3) CONTRADICTED — a label exists but other evidence refutes it, e.g. a run tagged with a commit whose tree does not contain the script that wrote the run's own artifact. Then write null HERE and the contradiction in `method`: which label was claimed, and what refuted it. Null and not the refuted label, because this field is read as 'the build this was measured against' and a value known to be false is worse than an absence — a later group-by would pool the rate with runs that really are that build, which is the pooling defect this field was added to prevent. The claim does not disappear; it moves to `method`, where it is prose a reader must read rather than a key a query will trust.

model_scope.description: What this rate is evidence ABOUT, not just which model happened to run it: a rate measured on one model is not evidence about another. Required when `status: "measured"` (Day-2 rev 5 Stage 1) — not enforced by a schema `required` here, since today's register predates this field on several measured rates; §48 (Stage 2) makes it bite by requiring `baseline.model_scope === current.model_scope` wherever `reduction_basis: "sampled"`, which is the mechanical form of the pooling rule and the check that would have caught a Haiku baseline read against a Sonnet current. Write the model id this rate is scoped to (e.g. `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`), or the literal `"model-independent"` for a structural count whose `model` is honestly null — never invent a model that did not measure it.
